I signed up for Redwood (self-serve) and briefly poked around the hosted API, but our engineering team needs a conversation about dedicated capacity for a pilot. Can we schedule a 45–60 minute deep-dive to walk through how Dedicated would handle our workload and the autoscaling/fallback behavior? Also curious about quantization tradeoffs and whether Redwood has guidance for batch-friendly prompt formats.

I'm copying our procurement lead once we have a time to lock.

Kimberly / Maria — quick technical note ahead of the call.

Thanks for the numbers, Maria. A couple of clarifying questions that will materially change the sizing:
- Concurrency distribution: is 300 req/s a sustained peak for minutes, or bursts that last seconds?
- Sequence-length mix: % of short (<64 tokens), medium (64–512), long (>512). If long is >10% we should include long-seq optimized nodes.
- Cacheability: are there large shared prefixes (e.g., system prompts, repeated instructions) that could be cached?
- Tolerance for quantization: are you okay with 4-bit/8-bit for most models if it reduces cost by ~2–3x, or do you require FP16 for fidelity?

I attached a quick throughput_estimate.csv that maps different node mixes to expected sustained req/s at p95 <250ms for a few common model families. If Maria can drop a few sample prompts (even 5) we can run a micro-benchmark in advance and bring real numbers to the demo.

Follow-ups on the logistics side:
- If procurement needs an NDA before a technical deep-dive, we can route our standard mutual NDA (attached draft: nda_stowell.pdf) to DocuSign.
- Monica, can you own pilot milestones / success criteria?

— Ben
